risk.label: Do not rely on this build

findings.title: Defined name points at a deleted range
findings.why: Any formula using this name is now pointing at nothing, and the failure can be masked by a cached value that still looks correct.
findings.fix: Re-point 'PriorYearTotal' at the intended range or delete it, then search for its uses and correct them.

findings.title: Circular reference (1 loop)
findings.why: A circular reference means the figure depends on itself. Excel resolves it iteratively, so the value drifts with every recalculation and is not reproducible from the inputs.
findings.fix: Break the loop. Identify the cell that should be an input rather than a calculation, and replace one leg of the cycle with a typed assumption placed outside the loop.

findings.title: Workbook depends on another file
findings.detail: References point outside this workbook. The files are Prior year P&L.xlsx.
findings.why: External links break silently. The recipient sees stale cached values, and any figure that came from the other file is no longer verifiable from this one.
findings.fix: Break the links. Paste the required values as labelled inputs on a source sheet, or rebuild the reference inside the workbook. Then check that no formula still contains a bracketed file name.

findings.title: Tie-out fails for Total revenue equals the sum of every product line
findings.detail: 'P&L'!B9-SUM('P&L'!B5:B8) evaluates to -404.00 against a tolerance of 0.50, so it is out by 404.00.
findings.why: Reconciliations exist because these two figures are supposed to agree. When they do not, at least one of them is wrong.
findings.fix: Trace both sides to their inputs and correct the one that is incomplete. Re-run after the fix.

findings.title: Typed value inside a calculated row
findings.detail: Row 16 is calculated across B16:M16 but these cells hold typed numbers, starting with H16=12500. The pattern at B16 would give H16 = 492.55, so the typed value is off by +12,007.45.
findings.why: A hardcoded number inside a calculated row is the most common way a model quietly stops tying. It survives every future update because nothing recalculates it.
findings.fix: Replace each typed value with the formula its neighbours use, or move the assumption to an input sheet and reference it so the override is visible and labelled.

findings.title: Cell shows a value but the formula resolves to an error
findings.detail: 1 cell(s) carry a stored number while the formula evaluates to an error. For example, P&L!B23 stores 1370 but ='Old workings v0'!B2 resolves to #REF!.
findings.why: The reader sees a plausible number. The moment anyone recalculates, or links to the cell from another model, it becomes an error or a blank. This is the most dangerous class of defect in a workbook that is about to be circulated.
findings.fix: Correct the formula at its source, then recompute and confirm the cell now shows the intended figure.

findings.title: Stored result does not match the formula
findings.detail: 2 cell(s) hold a cached value that disagrees with a recomputation of the formula. For example, P&L!B12 shows 99999 but =B9-B11 evaluates to 2175.0 (difference -97,824.00).
findings.why: The number on the page is not the number the formula produces. This happens when a file is written by a script or another tool, when a workbook is edited outside Excel, or when a calculation was interrupted. Every reader trusts the cached value, so the error travels silently.
findings.fix: Recompute in Excel (F9), save, and re-run. If the recomputation changes a figure you have already reported, treat the cached value as wrong and trace what changed.

findings.title: Total excludes the row or column next to its range
findings.detail: 12 total cells in row 9 sum B5:B7 but the row directly outside the range (B8:M8) holds a value of 404 and is otherwise part of the same block. The totals affected are B9, C9, D9, E9, F9, G9 (+6 more). The excluded values sum to 5,640.00.
findings.why: The classic broken model. A line is added after the total was built, the SUM range does not grow, and the figure is understated with no visible error. Nothing on the page looks wrong.
findings.fix: Confirm the block is meant to include it, then extend each total along its own axis, from B5:B7 to B5:B8 (for example B9 changes from =SUM(B5:B7) to =SUM(B5:B8)), or delete the orphan row if it should not be there.

findings.title: Hidden sheets carry content (1)
findings.detail: Not visible in the workbook tabs. They are Old workings.
findings.why: A sheet the reader cannot see is a place where inputs, workings or stale calculations survive review. Reviewers routinely miss them.
findings.fix: Unhide each sheet, decide whether it is load-bearing, and either label it as workings or delete it.

findings.title: Same block displayed as both percent and decimal
findings.detail: Row 21 holds 12 numbers, 11 formatted as percent and 1 as plain number. The ambiguous cells are I21. For example I21 displays as a plain 0.25.
findings.why: A cell showing 0.07 and a cell showing 7% read as different magnitudes even when they hold the same number. In a margin or growth block that is how an order-of-magnitude error survives review.
findings.fix: Apply one convention to the whole row, then re-check the dependent rows still foot after the change.

findings.title: Formula does not follow its row pattern
findings.detail: J5 differs from the pattern used by 10 other cells on the same row 5. The pattern is =B5*1.03, as at C5. The deviation is J5 =I5+0.03.
findings.why: Fill-across models rely on every cell in a period row being the same formula shifted. A deviation is either a deliberate exception that should be labelled or a copy-paste slip that will not survive the next roll-forward.
findings.fix: Compare each listed formula with the pattern next to it and either restore the pattern or add a note explaining the exception.

findings.title: Formulas have no stored results
findings.detail: 4 formula cells carry no cached value, e.g. P&L!B25, P&L!B27, P&L!G33, P&L!H33.
findings.why: The workbook has not been recalculated since it was last written by a tool or script. Any figures another system reads from it may be blank or stale, and no formula audit alone can confirm the expected result.
findings.fix: Open the workbook in Excel, let it calculate fully, save, and re-run this audit so the check can compare formula and result.

findings.title: Hidden rows or columns inside the used range
findings.why: Hidden rows and columns inside a data block are the standard way a period or entity is excluded from a total without anyone noticing.
findings.fix: Unhide and review each one, or delete it. If a column is hidden only for presentation, move it out of the data block.

findings.title: NOW() used 1 time
findings.why: NOW is volatile and changes every time the file recalculates. In an audit trail that means the reported figure cannot be reproduced from the file alone.
findings.fix: Replace with a fixed input or a non-volatile equivalent where possible, and document the assumption date where it cannot be avoided.
